Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral consolidation with multiple cystic lucencies (pseudocavitation), a radiographic pattern highly characteristic of pneumonic-type lung adenocarcinoma (formerly mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinoma). While infections can cause cavitation, the specific appearance of pseudocavitation within extensive consolidation strongly favors this malignancy over typical bacterial pneumonia or fungal infections.
